originality.rationale: Novelty is restricted to axis identifiability from ONE radius marginal (indeed from support plus one tail coefficient), not the joint or marginal distribution itself. The classical Dixon–Anderson real-compression joint law fully covers the underlying eigenvalue probability distribution, but the inspected statements do not establish observation reduction, a recoverable tail statistic or the inverse map. Distinct prior stereology, random-radius bounds and known one-spike laws were compared; older matrix and stereology priority remains a documented risk.

value.rationale: The inverse question is natural: whether one-dimensional observations of random central-section maximum radius identify a fully triaxial body. The answer gives a complete injectivity theorem and a constructive three-statistic recovery map, with the short-axis information residing in a sharp square-root tail amplitude. This is not a restatement of the general joint spectral law, whose observation includes the second restricted eigenvalue. No finite-sample estimator or stability theorem is claimed; the exact analytic inverse is itself the mathematical contribution.
